title: Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (METV): Portfolio Insights and 2026 Outlook
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
# Key Takeaways

* METV is a passively managed thematic ETF tracking the Ball Metaverse Index, holding 41 globally-listed equities spanning hardware, compute, networking, virtual platforms, payments, and content categories tied to the metaverse theme.
* The fund's portfolio is heavily concentrated in Technology Services (40%) and Electronic Technology (37%), with top holdings including [AAPL](https://tickeron.com/ticker/AAPL/), [RBLX](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RBLX/), [NVDA](https://tickeron.com/ticker/NVDA/), and [GOOGL](https://tickeron.com/ticker/GOOGL/), alongside indirect cryptocurrency exposure through Canadian-listed crypto staking ETFs.
* The metaverse investment theme is undergoing a structural evolution, shifting from speculative virtual worlds toward practical spatial computing, AI-integrated hardware, and enterprise applications.
* Recent performance has been shaped by a recovery in cryptocurrency prices, strength in semiconductor holdings, and improving user engagement metrics from key gaming-related constituents.
* Persistent fund outflows and an expense ratio of 0.59% remain considerations for investors evaluating thematic exposure in a maturing but still volatile segment.

# METV Fund Overview and Structure

The Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF seeks to track the performance, before fees and expenses, of the Ball Metaverse Index. Launched in June 2021 and issued by Roundhill Investments, METV is structured as a passive, non-diversified thematic ETF with an expense ratio of 0.59%. The fund held approximately $213 million in assets under management (AUM) across 41 holdings as of mid-2026.

The underlying index, developed by Ball Metaverse Research Partners, identifies companies engaged in activities that enable the metaverse across seven categories: Hardware, Compute, Networking, Virtual Platforms, Interchange Standards, Payments, and Content, Assets and Identity Services. Constituents are classified as pure-play, core, or non-core and weighted on a tiered basis, with individual issuer weights capped at 8% and category weights capped at 25%.

METV's portfolio is dominated by large-cap equities, with approximately 85% of assets in companies exceeding $12.9 billion in market capitalization. The top holdings reflect the fund's multi-sector approach: [Apple](https://tickeron.com/ticker/AAPL/) (7.3%), [Roblox](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RBLX/) (5.4%), [NVIDIA](https://tickeron.com/ticker/NVDA/) (4.8%), [Unity Software](https://tickeron.com/ticker/U/) (4.7%), and [Alphabet](https://tickeron.com/ticker/GOOGL/) (4.7%). Notably, the fund also holds Canadian-listed cryptocurrency staking ETFs—the 3iQ Ether Staking ETF and 3iQ Solana Staking ETF—which together represent approximately 9% of assets and provide indirect exposure to digital assets. Geographic exposure is predominantly North American, with roughly 65% allocated to U.S.-domiciled companies.

# The Maturing Metaverse Investment Landscape

The metaverse investment theme has matured considerably since the speculative peak of 2021-2022. Rather than focusing exclusively on immersive virtual worlds, the narrative has broadened to encompass spatial computing, augmented and mixed reality, AI-driven content generation, and the infrastructure layer—semiconductors, networking equipment, and cloud computing—that underpins these experiences. This evolution has made the theme more durable but also more diffuse, as many of the same companies driving metaverse development are also beneficiaries of the broader artificial intelligence buildout.

Enterprise adoption of mixed reality solutions has accelerated, with industrial manufacturers, automotive firms, and aerospace companies deploying immersive technologies for training, remote collaboration, and digital twin simulations. Meanwhile, the consumer-facing side of the theme remains anchored by gaming platforms like [Roblox](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RBLX/), which continues to report strong user engagement metrics, and by hardware ecosystems from companies such as [Apple](https://tickeron.com/ticker/AAPL/) and Meta Platforms.

The cryptocurrency component of METV's portfolio adds another layer of complexity. After a challenging second quarter of 2026—during which digital assets posted a third consecutive quarter of losses amid institutional outflows and capital rotation into AI equities—cryptocurrency markets showed signs of stabilization in early July. Bitcoin recovered toward $63,000 and Ethereum climbed back above $1,740, supported by a resumption of spot ETF inflows and a more dovish tone from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh regarding inflation risks. This crypto recovery has provided a tailwind for METV's indirect digital asset exposure.

Broader macroeconomic conditions remain mixed. While inflation concerns have moderated, U.S. Treasury yields have stayed elevated, with the 10-year yield holding above 4.5%. Geopolitical tensions, including renewed U.S.-Iran military exchanges, have periodically injected volatility into equity and commodity markets. For a thematic ETF like METV, which blends growth-oriented technology stocks with crypto-adjacent holdings, this environment has produced choppy but ultimately range-bound trading conditions.

# Recent Performance and What’s Driving It

METV's price action over recent months reflects the cross-currents affecting its diverse portfolio. After trading near $19.50 in early June, the ETF declined to approximately $17.32 by mid-June, pressured by weakness in cryptocurrency markets and broader risk-off sentiment. A subsequent recovery lifted shares back toward the $19 level by early July, representing a roughly 10% rebound from the monthly low.

Several identifiable drivers contributed to this recovery. [Roblox](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RBLX/) shares surged more than 12% in late June following an analyst upgrade that highlighted improving user engagement metrics and re-accelerating bookings growth. The gaming platform, which represents one of METV's largest pure-play metaverse holdings, benefited from strong concurrent user data and optimism around its age-verification rollout. Semiconductor holdings such as [NVIDIA](https://tickeron.com/ticker/NVDA/) and [AMD](https://tickeron.com/ticker/AMD/) continued to draw support from sustained AI infrastructure spending, even as Meta Platforms announced plans to manufacture its own custom AI chips—a development that boosted the broader semiconductor ecosystem.

The cryptocurrency leg of the portfolio also contributed positively. Bitcoin's 9% gain from the end of June through early July, coupled with five consecutive days of spot Bitcoin ETF inflows, helped lift the value of METV's crypto ETF holdings. Ethereum outperformed bitcoin over the same period, rising approximately 6% in a single week, which directly benefited the fund's Ether staking ETF position.

Despite the recent recovery, METV has experienced persistent net outflows. One-month net outflows totaled approximately $16 million as of mid-June, and the fund's AUM has declined from higher levels earlier in the year. The ETF's beta of 1.42 indicates amplified sensitivity to equity market movements, consistent with its growth-oriented, technology-heavy composition. On a quarterly basis, the fund posted a modest gain of approximately 4.8% through mid-June, underperforming the broader technology ETF category average of 21% over the same period, partly reflecting the drag from cryptocurrency exposure during a quarter when digital assets declined.

# Looking Ahead to the Rest of 2026

Several structural factors are likely to influence METV's trajectory through the remainder of 2026. The trajectory of cryptocurrency markets remains a primary variable. Sustained spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF inflows would support the fund's digital asset exposure, while a resumption of outflows or another leg down in crypto prices would create headwinds. The July 17 CLARITY Act hearing in the U.S. Senate represents a potential regulatory catalyst that could affect digital asset valuations and, by extension, METV's crypto-adjacent holdings.

The evolution of the metaverse theme itself will continue to shape the fund's narrative. The shift toward practical spatial computing applications and AI-integrated hardware—exemplified by Meta's custom AI chip plans and the ongoing enterprise adoption of digital twin technology—could broaden the theme's appeal beyond early adopters. However, the theme's diffuse nature means that METV's performance will remain heavily influenced by the fortunes of its largest holdings, many of which are mega-cap technology companies whose stock movements are driven by factors extending well beyond metaverse-specific developments.

Semiconductor demand, particularly for AI accelerators and high-bandwidth memory, is expected to remain robust, which should continue to benefit METV's significant Electronic Technology allocation. Conversely, any slowdown in AI infrastructure spending or a rotation away from growth stocks—potentially triggered by persistently elevated interest rates or an economic downturn—would disproportionately affect the fund given its growth-oriented composition and above-market beta.

Fund flows represent another important monitor. Thematic ETFs have generally faced redemption pressure as investors have rotated toward broad-market index funds and AI-specific strategies. A stabilization or reversal of METV's outflow trend would signal renewed investor conviction in the metaverse theme. Finally, regulatory developments affecting cryptocurrency ETFs, gaming platforms, and data privacy could introduce both opportunities and risks for the fund's diverse portfolio. Investors should watch for any changes to the Ball Metaverse Index methodology, particularly regarding the inclusion or weighting of cryptocurrency-related instruments, as these could alter the fund's risk profile.
